claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating is chemically homogeneous and lacks distinct Cu-rich grain-boundary phases.
Annealing the coating at approximately 700 °C for 1 hour will induce controlled Cu segregation to grain boundaries.
The induced Cu segregation will form Cu-rich intergranular films along the coating's grain boundaries.
The Cu-rich intergranular films will be softer than the surrounding HEA coating.
Cu-rich intergranular films will act as a lubricious phase during high-temperature sliding.
The lubricious Cu-rich films will reduce frictional energy dissipation and the friction coefficient.
The Cu-rich films will reduce local stress concentrations during sliding.
High local pressure at contacting asperities can cause plastic deformation and adhesion during sliding.
Reducing local stress concentrations will suppress the nucleation and propagation of severe localized plastic deformation, including shear bands.
The annealed, Cu-segregated coating will have a lower wear rate than the as-deposited coating.
The annealed, Cu-segregated coating will show more homogeneous microscopic deformation and fewer localized shear bands.
The predicted effects should hold during sliding at 600–700 °C because thermal activation in that range permits controlled Cu segregation.
The 600–700 °C regime can permit Cu segregation without complete phase degradation or wear-dominating unwanted oxidation.
Oxidation dynamics during prolonged high-temperature sliding may compete with the proposed Cu-segregation mechanism.
The wear benefit depends on the kinetics and morphology of Cu segregation.
